name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
summary: A green field with the Southern Cross in yellow stars, a yellow palm tree on a gold disc in the canton, and a yellow crescent in the centre.
origin: The flag was adopted by the shire council on 6 April 2004 after a competition. It has no official status nationally but is used by the local government.

symbols.name: Palm tree
symbols.description: A yellow coconut palm on a disc.

symbols.name: Crescent
symbols.meaning: The islands' Cocos Malay Muslim majority.

facts: The islands were privately owned by the Clunies-Ross family until 1978.
The territory has 27 coral islands, two of them inhabited.
clues: Green with a yellow palm, a crescent and the Southern Cross in yellow.
Its islands were once owned by a single family.
Its crescent represents a Muslim majority.
